rationale: Evidence from iteration 5 (sensors at y 0.07, kp 1.4, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.0; score 661.4, the best so far). The oval finished 20/20 at 1.98 s with oscillation 0.18. The s-bend finished 19/20 (up from 15/20) and its oscillation fell from 0.38 to 0.32, so the extra sensor lead helped the s-bend. The slalom did not move: progress 0.311 against 0.306 at y 0.05, still off_track in all 20 runs, max_error at the 0.064 mean, and oscillation low at 0.21. Lead is therefore not the slalom's limit. The Evaluator's rule for this pattern (slalom progress near 0.3 with low oscillation) points to speed through the slalom's sharp turns. Off-track is unavoidable at the current speed, and widening the body cannot raise the limit above 0.0575 m. Change: base_speed 1.0 to 0.9, with everything else unchanged (kp 1.4, kd 0.5, y 0.07, x positions, 16 mm footprints, sensor weights, line_loss last_direction). This is a single-variable step. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.31 and max_error below 0.06 on some runs, with the oval still finishing 20/20 (it has time margin at about 2 s). The s-bend completion time should rise from about 2.3 s to about 2.5 to 2.7 s, which is still under 3 s. Risk: if the s-bend completion time exceeds 2.9 s or finishes fall below 17/20, return base_speed to 1.0. Hypotheses to check next: (1) if slalom progress rises with max_error still at 0.06, the sharp turns need more speed reduction or a higher kd; (2) if slalom progress stays at 0.31 despite the lower speed, the limit is sensor reach at the sharpest bend, so the next step is y 0.075 or wider outer sensors. Measurements requested: per track completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors and noise_robustness.
